title: Germany – Gas-fitting installation work – Medizinische Gase (VE065), CVK, DHZC
description: Die Charité - Universitätsmedizin Berlin, Campus Virchow-Klinikum (CVK), Augustenburger Platz 1, 13353 Berlin, beabsichtigt die Errichtung eines zukunftsweisenden Neubaus für das Deutsche Herzzentrum der Charité (DHZC) im südwestlichen Bereich des Campus Virchow-Klinikum (CVK). In dem geplanten Neubau werden u. a. auch die Zentrale Sterilgutversorgung (ZSVA) und die Zentrale Notaufnahme (ZNA) untergebracht sowie auf dem Dach des Gebäudes ein Hubschrauberlandeplatz errichtet. Die Gesamtnutzfläche für den Neubau DHZC beträgt ca. 29.800 m² bei einer Bruttogrundrissfläche von ca. 75.600 m² und einem Bruttorauminhalt von ca. 355.000 m³. Es ist geplant, den Neubau als Hochbau mit 16 Obergeschossen sowie 2 Untergeschossen zu errichten. Für das Gebäude wird eine Nachhaltigkeitszertifizierung nach dem System der Deutschen Gesellschaft für Nachhaltiges Bauen (DGNB) in der Stufe "Gold" angestrebt. Gemäß Vorgabe der Medizintechnik sind Funktionsbereiche, Untersuchungs- und Behandlungszimmer sowie die Bereiche für Allgemein-, IMC-, ITS-Pflege mit Sauerstoff, medizinischer Druckluft und Vakuum zu versorgen. Ebenso sind in einigen wenigen Funktionsbereichen Entnahmestellen für Narkosegasabsaugungen (AGFS) und CO2 sowie eine technische Druckluft für Reinigungs-, Desinfektions- und Sterilisationsautomaten erforderlich. Es bestehen gesonderte Anforderungen nach dem Berliner Ausschreibungs- und Vergabegesetz (BerlAVG), siehe Vergabeunterlagen. Nähere Informationen können den auf der Vergabeplattform der Charité (https://vergabeplattform.charite.de) zur Verfügung gestellten Unterlagen entnommen werden.

title: Building America Subject Matter Expert Technical Support
description: **Please see Amendment 2 dated 10/30/2026.** **Please see Amendment 1 dated 10/15/2026.** NLR seeks to engage leading technical subject matter experts (SMEs) to help buildings industry stakeholders scale up and meet demand for lower-cost, high-quality buildings. SMEs will support DOE�s Building America program, both its just-launched new construction support program and existing support programs for building envelope retrofits. The new construction support program will provide technical assistance to help partners erect high-quality buildings faster and at lower cost, ultimately delivering savings to everyday Americans. NLR seeks leading subject matter experts (SMEs) in research, field validation, analysis, dissemination, and technical support efforts to help builders, manufacturers, contractors, and other industry stakeholders scale up and meet demand. This work will focus on factory optimization, product design and materials innovation, and digital tools and modeling. For envelope retrofits, this work will help reduce first costs and lower utility bills in existing homes by focusing on technical topics including, but not limited to, addressing moisture, humidity, and infiltration through envelope upgrades and whole-home solutions. Across both areas, SMEs will also conduct modeling and analysis, data collection, industry analysis, and market scaling support. This work will include knowledge transfer to provide actionable guidance and information to industry stakeholders. For over 30 years, DOE�s Building America Program has been a source of innovations and best practices needed to deliver affordable and efficient homes. NLR supports DOE�s Building America Program through scientific leadership and building science expertise to ensure high-quality, impactful results from Building America�s research efforts.

title: Corral G-Z Stewardship IRSC, Region 6, Fremont-Winema National Forest, Bly Ranger District, Bly , Oregon
description: Amendment 001: Posted 10/06/2026 - Changes Site Visit date from Thursday, October 22, 2026 to Thursday, October 29, 2026. Adds Project Spatial Data zip files. See attachments for SF30 with amended solicitation pages, and spatial data files. This is a combined synopsis/solicitation for commercial services prepared in accordance with FAR 12. This announcement constitutes the only solicitation; quotes are being requested, and a separate written solicitation will not be issued. Solicitation number 12363N26Q4181 is issued as a request for quotation (RFQ). This project follows the G to Z Integrated Resource Stewardship Contract (IRSC) model which is a unique approach that takes projects from signed NEPA decision and reintroduction of fire on the landscape. The Corral G-Z Integrated Resource Service Contract directly supports Executive Order 14225, the Immediate Expansion of American Timber Production, Secretary Rollins Memorandum 1078-006 and follows the direction put forth by Acting Associate Chief Chris French in producing timber volume, reducing hazardous fuels, providing wood fiber to struggling industries and supporting local economies surrounding the Fremont-Winema National Forest. The objectives of this project are 1) to restore forest health and vigor by reverting stand density and species composition to their historical range of variability, while also 2) mitigating the threat of catastrophic wildfire by reducing hazardous fuels. These objectives will be accomplished through the following: Professional Forestry: Completion of harvest layout, timber marking, timber volume determination and acre determination of harvest unit boundaries, and DxP prescription monitoring. Logging and Fuels Reduction: Cut and remove an estimated 191,379 tons of commercial timber on approximately 7,000 acres, and fuels reduction on approximately 17,000 acres. Removal will include ground-based logging systems utilizing whole tree yarding, cutting, skidding and decking sub-merchantable trees in plantations, fuel breaks and general stands. Cut and pile encroaching conifers in meadow areas and release cuts in whitebark pine stands. The associated North American Industrial Classification System (NAICS) code for this procurement is 113310 �logging, with a small business size standard of 500 employees. The product service code is F014. The government will award a Firm-Fixed Price (FFP) contract resulting from this combined synopsis/solicitation to the responsible quoter whose quote, conforming to the synopsis/solicitation, will be most advantageous to the government (as determined by the solicitation evaluation criteria). All responsible sources may submit a quotation which will be considered by the agency, and shall be valid for 60 days after the date of receipt for the solicitation.

title: TECHNICAL SERVICES for NRL 8100 DIV
description: The Naval Research Laboratory (NRL), Code 8124, Advanced Operations Section, intends to procure engineering and technical support services for the design, development, implementation, modification, maintenance, troubleshooting, and repair of specialized research and development equipment. The contractor shall provide qualified personnel, technical expertise, supervision, management, equipment, tools, materials, and other necessary resources to support operations at the NRL Code 8124 Pomonkey Facility in La Plata, Maryland, and an associated Outside Continental United States (OCONUS) facility. The required services include, but are not limited to: - Support and maintenance of full-motion and limited-motion parabolic antenna systems. - Radio frequency (RF), microwave, waveguide, coaxial, fiber-optic, and network transmission systems. - Electrical, mechanical, electromechanical, and control systems. - Precision fabrication, machining, installation, and modification of specialized equipment and components. - Radome, HVAC, dehumidification, and environmental-control systems. - Backup generators, uninterruptible power systems, telecommunications, CCTV, and related infrastructure. - Preventive and corrective maintenance, testing, calibration, and operational-readiness support. - Technical documentation and configuration management. The Government anticipates awarding a purchase order consisting of firm-fixed-price labor Contract Line Item Numbers (CLINs), with separately identified cost-no-fee CLINs for materials and travel. The anticipated period of performance consists of a twelve (12) month base period and four (4) twelve-month option periods. **NAICS Code:** 541330 - Engineering Services **Place of Performance:** Naval Research Laboratory, Code 8124, Pomonkey Facility, 7425 Bumpy Oak Road, La Plata, MD 20646, and an associated OCONUS facility. Interested vendors shall review the complete solicitation, including all attachments, for detailed performance requirements, personnel qualifications, quotation instructions, and evaluation criteria. **Solicitation Number:** N00173-27-Q-0002 **Quotation Due Date:** November 13, 2026 **Contracting Point of Contact:** Torrean J. Green Contract Specialist Naval Research Laboratory, Code 1330 Email: torrean.j.green.civ@us.navy.mil All questions concerning this solicitation shall be directed to the Contracting Point of Contact identified above.

title: Facility Weight Handling Equipment (WHE) Maintenance and Repair Services at Marine Corps Installation Pacific (MCI-PAC) Camp Smedley D. Butler Okinawa, Japan

The intent of this notice is to conduct market research and identify potential contractors that are capable of performing the work in Japan and interested in the Department of Navy�s requirement for Facility Weight Handling Equipment (WHE) Maintenance and Repair Services at Marine Corps Installation Pacific (MCI-PAC) Camp Smedley D. Butler Okinawa, Japan. The information will be used within the NAVFAC FE Contracting Division and will not be disclosed outside the agency. This notice does NOT constitute a request for proposal, request for quote, or invitation for bid. No reimbursement will be made for any costs associated with providing information in response to this announcement or any follow-up information requests. SERVICES DESCRIPTION: The proposed Facility WHE maintenance and repair services will require the contractor to provide all labor, supervision, management, tools, materials, equipment, facilities, transportation, incidental engineering, and other items necessary to perform WHE maintenance and repair services at Marine Corps Installation Pacific (MCI-PAC) Camp Smedley D. Butler Okinawa, Japan. (e.g., Camp Courtney, Camp Foster, Marine Corps Air Station (MCAS) Futenma, Camp Gonsalves, Camp Hansen, Camp Kinser, Camp Lester, Camp Schwab). The services anticipated: Service orders Preventive maintenance (PM) Inspection, Testing and Certification Program The anticipated contract type is a single award, Indefinite-Delivery Indefinite-Quantity (IDIQ) contract with Recurring and Non-Recurring work items. The anticipated period of performance is a twelve-month base period with four (4) one-year option periods. This notice is for information and planning purposes only and shall not be construed as a solicitation or as an obligation on the part of the Government to issue a Solicitation or award a contract. The Government does not intend to award a contract based on responses. Entities responding to this Sources Sought Notice should submit the minimum information necessary for the Government to make a determination that adequate business entities exist that are capable of satisfying the Government�s requirements. The North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) Code is 811310 Commercial and Industrial Machinery and Equipment. It is requested that interested firms capable of providing the requested services submit a brief capabilities statement package (no more than 12 single sided pages, including attachments, single spaced, 12 point font minimum) demonstrating ability to perform the requested services. The documentation shall address the following: COMPANY PROFILE to include all of the following: (1) Company name and address; (2) Company point of contact (including title, telephone number and email address); and (3) SAM Unique Entity Identifier (UEI) and CAGE code. RELEVANT EXPERIENCE: Provide a minimum of one (1) or up to a maximum of five (5) projects indicating your experience in providing services for the requirement stated above. Please indicate number of years of experience and location of work. SUBCONTRACTORS: If known, provide established subcontractor arrangements or partnerships with other companies (Optional). LICENSE/CERTIFICATIONS: Indicate any applicable local/and or industry certification your company or employee possess relevant to this procurement. MISC INFO: Provide anything pertinent to this industry and/or type of work, in general, that the Government should consider. Interested firms may submit information using the form provided under separate file titled �Sources Sought � Contractor Information Form (attachment 1)� to demonstrate capabilities, capacity and experience. Notifications of interest must be submitted in writing via email; phone calls will not be accepted. The contractor shall provide qualified personnel, technical expertise, supervision, management, equipment, tools, materials, and other necessary resources to support operations at the NRL Code 8124 Pomonkey Facility in La Plata, Maryland, and an associated Outside Continental United States (OCONUS) facility. The required services include, but are not limited to: - Support and maintenance of full-motion and limited-motion parabolic antenna systems. - Radio frequency (RF), microwave, waveguide, coaxial, fiber-optic, and network transmission systems. - Electrical, mechanical, electromechanical, and control systems. - Precision fabrication, machining, installation, and modification of specialized equipment and components. - Radome, HVAC, dehumidification, and environmental-control systems. - Backup generators, uninterruptible power systems, telecommunications, CCTV, and related infrastructure. - Preventive and corrective maintenance, testing, calibration, and operational-readiness support. - Technical documentation and configuration management. The Government anticipates awarding a purchase order consisting of firm-fixed-price labor Contract Line Item Numbers (CLINs), with separately identified cost-no-fee CLINs for materials and travel. The anticipated period of performance consists of a twelve (12) month base period and four (4) twelve-month option periods. **NAICS Code:** 541330 - Engineering Services **Place of Performance:** Naval Research Laboratory, Code 8124, Pomonkey Facility, 7425 Bumpy Oak Road, La Plata, MD 20646, and an associated OCONUS facility. Interested vendors shall review the complete solicitation, including all attachments, for detailed performance requirements, personnel qualifications, quotation instructions, and evaluation criteria. **Solicitation Number:** N00173-27-Q-0002 **Quotation Due Date:** November 13, 2026 **Contracting Point of Contact:** Torrean J. Green Contract Specialist Naval Research Laboratory, Code 1330 Email: torrean.j.green.civ@us.navy.mil All questions concerning this solicitation shall be directed to the Contracting Point of Contact identified above.

title: Facility Weight Handling Equipment (WHE) Maintenance and Repair Services at Marine Corps Installation Pacific (MCI-PAC) Camp Smedley D. Butler Okinawa, Japan
description: ***THIS IS A SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE ONLY*** Naval Facilities Engineering Systems Command Far East (NAVFAC FE) ROICC Camp Butler is conducting a Sources Sought Notice. The intent of this notice is to conduct market research and identify potential contractors that are capable of performing the work in Japan and interested in the Department of Navy�s requirement for Facility Weight Handling Equipment (WHE) Maintenance and Repair Services at Marine Corps Installation Pacific (MCI-PAC) Camp Smedley D. title: Corral G-Z Stewardship IRSC, Region 6, Fremont-Winema National Forest, Bly Ranger District, Bly , Oregon
description: Amendment 002: Posted 10/14/2026 - Revises Pages 5 and 6 of the Solicitation Schedule of Items. Quanties for Item 14, 16 and 21 are revised. Adds Grizzly project area spatial data for "no treatment areas." Replaces Grizzly Treatment Area Map. See attachments for SF30 with amended solicitation pages 5 and 6, spatial data zip file and new Grizzly Project Area Map. Amendment 001: Posted 10/06/2026 - Changes Site Visit date from Thursday, October 22, 2026 to Thursday, October 29, 2026. Adds Project Spatial Data zip files. See attachments for SF30 with amended solicitation pages, and spatial data files. This is a combined synopsis/solicitation for commercial services prepared in accordance with FAR 12. This announcement constitutes the only solicitation; quotes are being requested, and a separate written solicitation will not be issued. Solicitation number 12363N26Q4181 is issued as a request for quotation (RFQ). This project follows the G to Z Integrated Resource Stewardship Contract (IRSC) model which is a unique approach that takes projects from signed NEPA decision and reintroduction of fire on the landscape. The Corral G-Z Integrated Resource Service Contract directly supports Executive Order 14225, the Immediate Expansion of American Timber Production, Secretary Rollins Memorandum 1078-006 and follows the direction put forth by Acting Associate Chief Chris French in producing timber volume, reducing hazardous fuels, providing wood fiber to struggling industries and supporting local economies surrounding the Fremont-Winema National Forest. The objectives of this project are 1) to restore forest health and vigor by reverting stand density and species composition to their historical range of variability, while also 2) mitigating the threat of catastrophic wildfire by reducing hazardous fuels. These objectives will be accomplished through the following: Professional Forestry: Completion of harvest layout, timber marking, timber volume determination and acre determination of harvest unit boundaries, and DxP prescription monitoring. Logging and Fuels Reduction: Cut and remove an estimated 191,379 tons of commercial timber on approximately 7,000 acres, and fuels reduction on approximately 17,000 acres. Removal will include ground-based logging systems utilizing whole tree yarding, cutting, skidding and decking sub-merchantable trees in plantations, fuel breaks and general stands. Cut and pile encroaching conifers in meadow areas and release cuts in whitebark pine stands. The associated North American Industrial Classification System (NAICS) code for this procurement is 113310 �logging, with a small business size standard of 500 employees. The product service code is F014. The government will award a Firm-Fixed Price (FFP) contract resulting from this combined synopsis/solicitation to the responsible quoter whose quote, conforming to the synopsis/solicitation, will be most advantageous to the government (as determined by the solicitation evaluation criteria). All responsible sources may submit a quotation which will be considered by the agency, and shall be valid for 60 days after the date of receipt for the solicitation.

Detalii suplimentare se regăsesc în Caietul de sarcini. Numărul de zile până la care se pot solicita clarificări înainte de data limită de depunere a ofertelor este de 20 zile. A zárt rendszer alkalmazásával elkészített valamennyi citosztatikus készítmény, beleértve az infúziós zsákok/palackok, valamint gyógyszerrel előkészített, felhasználásra kész fecskendő + adapter egységek, azaz bólusok is egyaránt, a zárt rendszer különböző komponenseinek eltávolítása nélkül alkalmasak legyenek az Ajánlatkérő által alkalmazott csőposta rendszerben történő szállításra: méretük tegye lehetővé a 115 x 330 mm hasznos küldeményméretű szállítókapszulában történő biztonságos elhelyezést, és szállítást. A zárt rendszerek megrendelése általában havi egyszer történik, maximum 2 alkalommal. A hónap elején. A zárt rendszerek rendelési mennyisége az előző hónapban a kemoterápiás kezelések függvényében változhat. Konszignációs raktár létrehozása nem szükséges. Ajánlatkérő rögzíti, hogy átlagosan a következő megrendelései vannak havi szinten: 1. tétel: Ampulla adapter havi mennyiség: 1000-1200 db/hó 2. tétel: Infúziós palackhoz/zsákhoz való adapter: 1000-1200 db/hó 3. tétel: Fecskendő adapter luer-lock csatlakozással:400-600 db/hó 4. tétel: Luer-lock adapter: 30-60db/hó 5. tétel: Katéter adapter: 30-60 db/ hó Fentiekre tekintettel határozta meg ajánlatkérő az alkalmassági követelményt.

title: Romania – Other community, social and personal services – Servicii de training în comunicare, pe teme legate de finanțările europene, în cadrul proiectului „Rețeaua națională a comunicatorilor - asigurarea amplificării mesajelor pentru promovarea investițiilor europene”, Cod SMIS 338369/2.070
description: Acordul-cadru va asigura organizarea unor programe de formare în domeniul comunicării (training-uri în comunicare), destinate următoarelor categorii de participanți: • personalului de conducere din cadrul MIPE, respectiv demnitari, înalți funcționari publici, directori generali, directori și șefi de serviciu, având în vedere rolul acestora în reprezentarea instituției și în asigurarea imaginii acesteia (purtători de imagine), precum și faptul că funcția de comunicare reprezintă o componentă a procesului de management; • personalului din cadrul DGCCI (Direcția Generală Comunicare și Cooperare Internațională), având în vedere atribuțiile acestuia în domeniul comunicării instituționale și al informării publice - inclusiv în ceea ce privește comunicarea cu mass-media și diseminarea informațiilor către publicul țintă al programelor finanțate din FEN 2021–2027 gestionate de MIPE; • membrilor Rețelei Naționale a Comunicatorilor, cu condiția ca aceștia să nu fi participat anterior la programe de formare cu tematică similară, finanțate din alte fonduri publice europene sau naționale. Training-urile vor avea loc în regiunile de dezvoltare ale României, în perioada 2026-2029, vor fi în număr de 5, cu maxim 30 de participanți/training. Activitatea de organizare a sesiunilor de training include asigurarea componentei logistice pentru asigurarea experților formatori pentru sesiunile de training, a secretariatului tehnic, asigurarea cazării 6 nopți pentru maxim 30 de persoane (respectiv 25 de cursanți/ sesiune și 5 persoane responsabile de organizare din partea Autorității Contractante, mic dejun inclus), asigurarea serviciilor de catering pentru maxim 30 de persoane/ sesiune, închirierea sălii de conferințe pentru 5 zile/ sesiune, asigurarea personalului tehnic necesar pe durata desfășurării sesiunii de training, tipărirea și distribuirea suportului de curs, amenajarea locației evenimentului cu materiale de signalistică, realizarea materialelor de signalistică, asigurarea serviciilor de transport. Valoarea estimată: bugetul maxim estimat al acordului-cadru este de 1.180.291,67 RON fără TVA. Bugetul minim estimat al acordului-cadru este de 236.058,33 RON fără TVA. Valoarea estimată minimă a unui contract subsecvent: 236.058,33 RON fără TVA. Valoarea maximă estimată a celui mai mare contract subsecvent: 708.175 RON fără TVA. Autoritatea contractantă estimează încheierea a minim 1 contract subsecvent, maxim 5 contracte subsecvente. Tipul procedurii de achizitie: Procedura proprie Posibilitatea depunerii de oferte alternative: Nu pot fi depuse oferte alternative. Legislația aplicată • OMIPE nr. 555/24.03.2025 privind aprobarea normelor interne privind atribuirea contractelor de achiziție publică/acordurilor-cadru organizate prin procedura de atribuire aplicabilă în cazul serviciilor sociale şi al altor servicii specifice. • LEGEA NR. 98/2016 privind achizitiile publice, cu modificarile si completarile ulterioare; • HOTĂRÂREA GUVERNULUI nr. 395/2016 pentru aprobarea Normelor metodologice de aplicare a prevederilor referitoare la atribuirea contractului de achiziţie publică/acordului-cadru din Legea nr. 98/2016 privind achiziţiile publice, cu modificarile si completarile ulterioare; Oferta câștigătoare va fi cea care va obține punctajul total cel mai mare. Criteriul de atribuire aplicat de Autoritatea Contractantă pentru această procedură este „Cel mai bun raport calitate-preț” în conformitate cu art.187, alin.(3), lit. a) din Legea nr. 98/2016 privind achizițiile publice, cu modificările și completările ulterioare. Autoritatea contractantă va încheia acordul cadru cu operatorul economic, a cărui ofertă admisibilă a fost clasată pe primul loc în urma aplicării criteriului de atribuire - cel mai bun raport calitate/preț. În cazul în care 2 oferte sunt clasate pe primul loc, au punctaje egale, departajarea se va face având în vedere punctajul obținut la factorii de evaluare în ordinea descrescătoare a ponderilor acestora. În situația în care egalitatea se menține, autoritatea contractantă va solicita operatorilor economici respectivi, pentru departajare, transmiterea unei noi propuneri financiare, în vederea stabilirii clasamentului final. Se solicită operatorilor economici să-și păstreze valabilitatea ofertei 6 luni de la data limită de depunere a ofertelor. Durata acordului-cadru: 37 luni de la momentul semnării contractului de către ultima parte, dar nu mai tarziu de 30.11.2029. Garanția de participare : Nu este cazul. Garanția de bună execuție: Garanția de bună execuție: se solicită constituirea garanției de bună execuție în valoare de 5 % din valoarea contractului fără TVA. Perioada de valabilitate a garanţiei de bună execuție va fi egală cu durata contractului subsecvent. Data limită pentru depunerea ofertei: 17.11.2026 (minim 30 zile de la data transmiterii spre publicare), ora 23:59 la adresa de e-mail: cristinel.cerbu@mfe.gov.ro. Data limită pentru transmiterea solicitărilor de clarificări: cu 20 zile inainte de termenul de depunere, ora 23:59. Data la care autoritatea contractantă va răspunde consolidat la solicitările de clarificări: cu minim 10 zile inainte de termenul de depunere, ora 23:59. Toate informatiile privind participarea la prezenta procedura precum si setul de documente aferente se regasesc pe site-ul MIPE (https://mfe.gov.ro/invitatii-de-participare/) la sectiunea Interes Public/Achizitii publice/Invitatii de participare. Toate clarificarile/modificarile la documentatia de atribuire se vor publica pe site-ul MIPE, in aceeasi sectiune. Ca atare operatorii economici interesati vor consulta site-ul MIPE pentru informatii complete legate de prezenta procedura.

title: Bulgaria – Technical inspection services – Доставка на специализиран прибор и провеждане на контрол на основно оборудване на I-ви контур на 5 и 6 блок по метода на кинетичното индентиране
description: Предмет на настоящата обществена поръчка е да се достави съвременна автоматизирана система (по нататък за краткост "Уред") за измерване на механичните характеристики на металите по диаграмата на вдлъбването (метод на кинетичното индентиране) на оборудване. Дейностите следва да бъдат извършени по метода на кинетичната индентация в съответствие с БДС EN ISO 14577-1:2015 г. или еквивалентно/и. ​​​​​​​Етапи и обеми при изпълнение на работите: Етап 1 - Доставка на Уред, в съответствие с БДС EN ISO 14577-1:2015 г. или еквивалентно/и, включително един комплект резервни инструменти и принадлежности (ЗИП); Етап 2 - Провеждане на измервания на първият (5 или 6) ЕБ на основния метал и метала на заварените съединения без вземане на проби – измерване на твърдост по Бринел и определяне на механичните свойства по метода на кинетичното индентиране, на следното оборудване на блока: • трети главен циркулационен тръбопровод; • КН и съединителен тръбопровод на КН; • втори ПГ; • горен блок, корпус на реактора, опорен пръстен на реакторната установка. Етап 3 - На база получените резултати от измерването на КСК на първия (5 или 6) ЕБ изготвяне на Технически отчет. Етап 4 - Оказване на техническа помощ на обучения персонал на АЕЦ “Козлодуй” при провеждането на измерване на механичните характеристики на металите по диаграмата на вдлъбването на следното оборудване от втория (5 или 6) ЕБ: • първи главен циркулационен тръбопровод; • КН и съединителен тръбопровод на КН; • първи ПГ; • горен блок, корпус на реактора, опорен пръстен на реакторната установка. description: Предмет на обществената поръчка e „Доставка на хранителни продукти за детските заведения и Домашен социален патронаж на територията на Община Божурище“, по следните обособени позиции: Обособена позиция № 1 „Други пакетирани хранителни продукти”; Обособена позиция № 2 „Консерви – плодове и зеленчуци”; Обособена позиция № 3 „Месо и месни изделия”; Обособена позиция № 4 „Мляко и млечни изделия”; Обособена позиция № 5 „Плодове и зеленчуци – пресни и замразени”; Обособена позиция № 6 „Хляб и тестени изделия”. Пълното описание на хранителните продукти и техните ориентировъчни количества, необходими на Възложителя са описани в Технически спецификации – специфични изисквания към хранителните продукти, неразделна част от настоящите условия. КОЛИЧЕСТВАТА, описани в Техническата спецификация – специфични изисквания към хранителните продукти, са приблизително необходимите за 12 (дванадесет) месеца и са съобразени със заложените финансови средства в бюджета на Възложителя. Количествата и асортимента (видовете хранителни продукти), посочени в техническите спецификации, са индикативни (прогнозни) и не пораждат задължение за Възложителя да ги заявява - закупува в пълен обем. В рамката на договорената обща максимална стойност за поръчката, Възложителят има право да завишава или намалява количествата от даден хранителен продукт, както и да не заявява асортимент съобразно изискванията и предписанията на държавни контролни органи и нормативните документи, регламентиращи тази дейност, както и съобразно своите нужди до размера на общата стойност на поръчката, посочена в договора за доставка, сключен с Възложителя. Договорът за обществената поръчка се сключва на посочената от възложителя прогнозна стойност за нея, която се явява максимално допустимата стойност, до която възложителят може да заявява и купува хранителни продукти по предложените от участника единични цени. Забележка: За целия срок на договора Изпълнителя се задължава да доставя хранителни продукти с характеристики, марки и производители, съгласно декларираното в техническото му предложение. Изискванията на Възложителя относно изпълнението на предмета на поръчката се съдържат в: Техническа спецификация – разяснения; Технически спецификации (приложени отделно за всяка една от обособените позиции) – специфични изисквания към доставяните хранителни продукти, които са приложени към настоящите указания за участие и съставляват неразделна част от документацията за обществената поръчка, като следва да се четат като едно цяло.

title: France – Systems and technical consultancy services – Accompagnement à la sécurisation, à la modernisation et à la gouvernance de l'environnement Microsoft 365 de l'association Action Sociale Finance Restauration (ASFR)
description: La consultation a pour objet de contractualiser les prestations d'accompagnement à la sécurisation, à la modernisation et à la gouvernance de l'environnement Microsoft 365 de l'ASFR. L'ASFR a engagé la modernisation de son environnement de messagerie et de collaboration avec une migration Exchange / Microsoft 365 réalisée en 2025. L'environnement reste hybride avec Active Directory on-premises et Entra ID. Les audits de cybersécurité 2024 puis l'audit Microsoft 365 / Active Directory du 29/06/2026 ont identifié des écarts importants sur la gestion des identités et des privilèges, Entra Connect, la sécurité des postes, la protection de la messagerie, la gouvernance SharePoint/OneDrive/Teams, la supervision et la résilience. Le dernier audit estime un score global de conformité de 28/100 et recommande une remédiation prioritaire des non-conformités critiques. Le besoin porte sur un programme unique de transformation Microsoft 365, découpé en trois lots complémentaires et coordonnés. Le titulaire devra sécuriser et fiabiliser l'hybridation et les identités, moderniser la gestion et la sécurisation des postes de travail, puis mettre en place une gouvernance, une supervision et une amélioration continue de Microsoft 365. Le programme devra également traiter les reliquats documentés de la migration 2025, notamment la vérification de l'architecture hybride et de la déshybridation, et assurer un transfert de compétences vers l'équipe IT.

title: Poland – Natural gas – Zakup w ramach umowy kompleksowej paliwa gazowego i jego dystrybucji na potrzeby jednostek organizacyjnych Miasta Kalisza i innych podmiotów w roku 2027
description: 1. Przedmiotem zamówienia jest kompleksowa dostawa paliwa gazowego wraz z usługą dystrybucji paliwa gazowego, to jest gazu wysokometanowego o symbolu E do punktów poboru gazu jednostek organizacyjnych Miasta Kalisz i innych podmiotów na potrzeby wspólnego zamówienia prowadzonego na podstawie art. 37 ust. 2, art. 38 ust. 1 oraz art. 41 ustawy Prawo zamówień publicznych, realizowana na podstawie umowy kompleksowej, o której mowa w art. 5 ust. 3 ustawy z dnia 10 kwietnia 2007r. Prawo energetyczne i w ramach usługi kompleksowej w rozumieniu art. 3 pkt 30 ustawy Prawo energetyczne. 2.Podmioty objęte niniejszym postępowaniem, zwane dalej w SWZ „Odbiorcami Końcowymi” w imieniu i na rzecz których Miasto Kalisz zawrze na podstawie art. 38 ust. 1 i art. 41 ustawy Prawo zamówień publicznych umowę na zakup w ramach umowy kompleksowej paliwa gazowego i jego dystrybucji w roku 2027 wskazane zostały w załączniku nr 3 do umowy pn. „Wykaz zamawiających”. 3. Zakres zamówienia obejmuje sprzedaż i świadczenie usługi dystrybucji paliwa gazowego do punktów poboru gazu – dla budynków, lokali i obiektów użytkowych, dla których płatnikiem faktur za gaz są 43 jednostki organizacyjne Miasta Kalisza i 3 inne podmioty na potrzeby wspólnego zamówienia, kwalifikujące się jako odbiorcy: 1) uwzględnieni w art. 62b ust. 1 pkt 2 ustawy Prawo energetyczne, 2) nie uwzględnieni w art. 62b ust. 1 pkt 2 ustawy Prawo energetyczne. 4. Umowa wejdzie w życie z dniem podpisania. Natomiast dostawa paliwa gazowego rozpocznie się od 01.01.2027r., z zastrzeżeniem, że nie wcześniej niż po spełnieniu warunku skutecznego wypowiedzenia lub zakończenia obecnie obowiązującej umowy kompleksowej na dostawę paliwa gazowego oraz po pozytywnie przeprowadzonej procedurze zmiany sprzedawcy dla każdego punktu poboru. Przeprowadzenie procedury zmiany sprzedawcy leży po stronie Wykonawcy. Jako datę zakończenia dostaw paliwa gazowego wskazuje się 31.12.2027r. Wskazanie daty wykonania umowy jest uzasadnione koniecznością zakończenia wszelkich działań merytorycznych do końca roku budżetowego, ponieważ zadanie jest jednoroczne. 5. Szczegółowy opis przedmiotu zamówienia oraz pozostałe warunki realizacji zamówienia znajdują się w Specyfikacji Warunków Zamówienia (SWZ) i załącznikach do niej. 6. Zamawiający może skorzystać z prawa opcji przy następujących warunkach i założeniach: 1) w maksymalnej wartości do: 1.509.885,91 PLN netto; 2) prawo opcji może polegać na zwiększeniu ilości dostarczonego gazu ponad ilość objętą zamówieniem podstawowym (pkt 4.6 SWZ) w trakcie trwania umowy, 3) do prawa opcji stosuje się zapisy SWZ, załączników do SWZ oraz zapisy umowy o zamówienie i rozlicza jak umowę podstawową; 4) do prawa opcji zostanie przyjęta wartość wynagrodzenia - cena jednostkowa za paliwo gazowe/ stawka akcyzy/ stawka opłaty zmiennej/stałej obowiązująca w zawartej umowie określona na chwilę skorzystania z prawa opcji; 5) prawo opcji uruchamiane jest jednostronnym oświadczeniem woli zamawiającego, skierowanym do wykonawcy w terminie obowiązywania umowy w sprawie zamówienia i będzie miało zastosowanie w przypadku konieczności zapewnienia ciągłości świadczenia kompleksowej dostawy gazu i usługi dystrybucji lub rozszerzenia zakresu tej dostawy i usługi/ czynności; 6) wykonawca nie ma prawa żądania od Zamawiającego skorzystania z prawa opcji ani żądania zwiększenia lub zmniejszenia jego zakresu; 7) wielkość i zakres zamówienia zleconego w ramach prawa opcji ustala Zamawiający z uwzględnieniem powyższych zasad.

title: J065--PM Stealthstation S8 Service Contract
description: SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE This is a Sources Sought NOTICE (SSN) ONLY. The U.S. Government is conducting market research only to determine the availability of qualified sources capable of providing StealthStation S8 Preventative Maintenance. Potential Contractors are invited to provide a response via e-mail to Contract Specialist at tracy.heath@va.gov by November 16, 2026, 18:00 (PT). Responses will be used to determine the appropriate strategy for a potential acquisition. Please clearly identify any information your company considers sensitive or proprietary. This notice is issued solely for information and planning purposes - it does not constitute a Request for Quotation (RFQ), or a promise to issue an RFQ in the future. This notice does not commit the U.S. Government to contract for any supply or service. Further, the U.S. Government is not seeking quotes, or proposals at this time and will not accept unsolicited quotes in response to this source sought synopsis. The U.S. Government will not pay for any information or administrative costs incurred in response to this notice. Submittals will not be returned to the responder. Not responding to this notice does not preclude participation in any future RFQ, if any is issued. BACKGROUND: The Portland VA Medical Center has a requirement for a preventative maintenance service contract for the Stealthstation S8 stereotactic units to ensure proper operation. NAICS: 811210, Electronic and Precision Equipment Repair and Maintenance Interested potential Contractors please provide the following. 1) Company Name, address, point of contact, phone number, email address, and UEI Please indicate business size: Small Disadvantage Business (SDB)____ 8(a)____ Historically Underutilized Business Zone (HUBZone)____ Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Business (SDVOSB)____ Veteran-Owned Small Business (VOSB)_____ Economically Disadvantaged Women-Owned Small Business (EDWOSB)_____ Women-Owned Small Business concerns (WOSB)_____ Small Business_____ Large Business_____ Please state if you possess a Federal Supply Schedule (FSS)____. 2) Please submit a brief capability statement (maximum three pages) with enough information to demonstrate to the Veterans Affairs that you have enough resources, personnel, and experience to perform StealthStation S8 preventative maintenance as required in the attached Draft Statement of Work. **Draft Statement of Work STATEMENT OF WORK The Department of Veterans Affairs Portland VA Medical Center 3510 SW US Veterans Hospital Rd. Portland, OR 97239 General Requirements: Vendor to provide parts, labor, and travel to repair, maintain, and keep the existing Medtronic Stealthstation S8 units in good working order, meeting all OEM specifications for operation throughout the term of the contract. All parts shall be OEM parts only and repairs, maintenance, and calibration shall be performed by system product coordinators (OEM Trained) or by the OEM (MEDTRONIC) representatives. Serial Numbers: N30072021 S8 with EM (PN SERVICEC1-S8MCT21); N30072629 S8 with EM (PN SERVICEC1-S8MCT21) Planned (scheduled) preventative maintenance will be scheduled in advance with Biomedical Engineering on behalf of the service. Software maintenance releases and software upgrade releases (software enhancements and/or features) will be included at no extra cost. Hours of coverage will be Monday through Friday, 7AM to 4PM PST. This is for a Base Year contract for the Period of Performance of 11/19/2026 011/18/2027. Performance Monitoring The tasks are well defined and can, therefore, be easily monitored by the Government point of contact (POC), who shall represent the government for this process. The contractor performance will be monitored and the work certified by the POC. The POC will assure contractor quality by routine inspections, product sampling, and monitoring of work while work is being performed. Security Requirements All contractor employees will be escorted and monitored by a VA employee when onsite. The process to obtain a background check of the responsible FSE will be started on first arrival. Other Pertinent Information or Special Considerations. None Inspection and Acceptance Criteria. The POC is responsible for certifying that the work done under this contract is performed to standard. The POC is also responsible to assure the inspection and acceptance of products provided incidental to services. Place of Performance. Work will primarily be performed at the PVAMC. Period of Performance. 11/19/26 through 11/18/27. Delivery Schedule. SOW Task# Deliverable Title Format Number Calendar Days After CO Start 1 Calibration Certificates Contractor determined service report, but must meet required calibration standards 1 hard copy, 1 emailed copy Within 10 days after completion of work. 2 Invoice for work Contractor determined format. 1 hard copy or 1 emailed copy Within 30 days of completion of work.

title: 129 CEF - AVB Maintenance Services
description: This Sources Sought Posting is being issued in accordance with Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul (RFO) Part 10, Market Research. The purpose of this posting is to gain knowledge of potential sources for this service including interested Small Business Concerns. Its sole purpose is to provide information for planning and market research only and shall not be construed as either a solicitation or obligation on the part of the Government. The Government welcomes responses from all interested parties; however, no decision or award of contract will be made based on responses from industry. The Government will not pay for the preparation of, nor the subsequent use of, information submitted in response to this Sources Sought. Respondents will not be notified of the outcome of the Government�s review of the information received. Additionally, the Government does not intend to hold discussions concerning this Sources Sought with any interested parties but reserves the right to contact vendors if additional information is required for clarifications as it pertains to the Sources Sought. The 129th Rescue Wing at Moffett ANGB, CA, requires the provision of monthly, quarterly, and annual preventative maintenance and inspection services for two Delta Scientific DSC501 wedge barriers, one hydraulic pumping unit, and associated equipment in accordance with the attached draft Performance Work Statement. The scope is expected to include utility verification; site verification and layout; clearing, grubbing, and limited demolition; excavation and earthwork; export and disposal of excavated soil; irrigation modification; construction of an oval/elliptical concrete display pad; aircraft support features; anchoring/mooring features; static grounding; evaluation and installation of lightning-protection measures; solar-powered perimeter lighting; grading and stormwater drainage improvements; and landscape restoration of disturbed areas. The NAICS code for this requirement is 811310, Commercial and Industrial Machinery and Equipment (except Automotive and Electronic) Repair and Maintenance. The Small Business Administration size standard for small businesses in this industry is $12,500,000. Instructions to Vendors All interested concerns will submit a written notice, not to exceed five (5) pages, stating the concern�s positive intention to submit a proposal as a prime contractor no later than the deadline posted with this notice. Responses to this Sources Sought should include the following information: A positive statement of intent to submit a proposal as a prime contractor, A listing of projects completed during the past five (5) years for both Government and private industry. The list should provide the type of service, dollar value, contract number, location, and point of contact. Also, please indicate whether the firm was a prime or subcontractor�if the firm was a subcontractor, please provide a point of contact with the prime contractor, A brief outline of resources, subcontractors, and key personnel that would be used to accomplish the contract, and Demonstration of the firm�s socioeconomic status (i.e., SB, 8(a), HUBZone, EDWOSB, WOSB, SDVOSB, etc.), and size. If adequate small business firms are not available for adequate competition for this project, it may be advertised as an unrestricted solicitation. Submit responses directly to austin.breault.1@us.af.mil; telephone calls and facsimile responses will not be honored. Please reference the Notice ID and project title in the subject of your message. Please limit your responses to standard documents (i.e., Microsoft Office, Adobe PDF, etc.). Do not send compressed (i.e., .zip or .exe extension) or other file types as they will be stripped from your message.

title: NIH Scientific & Technical Expertise & Acquisition Management (STEAM)
description: SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE NIH SCIENTIFIC & TECHNICAL EXPERTISE ACQUISITION & MANAGEMENT (STEAM) Sources Sought Reference Number: 75N98027R00012 Proposed NAICS Code and Size Standard: 541990 � All Other Professional, Scientific and Technical Services; $19.5 million in average annual receipts Sources Sought Notice Information Introduction This is a Small Business Sources Sought notice. This is NOT a solicitation for proposals, proposal abstracts, or quotations. The purpose of this notice is to obtain information regarding: (1) the availability and capability of qualified small business sources; (2) their small business and applicable socioeconomic status, including HUBZone, service-disabled veteran-owned, veteran-owned, 8(a), woman-owned, and small disadvantaged business status; and (3) their size classification relative to the proposed North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code. Responses will assist the Government in determining the appropriate acquisition method, including whether a full or partial small business set-aside is appropriate. Interested small businesses may respond for Task Area A (Professional Services), Task Area B (Highly Specialized Scientific Services), or both. Respondents should identify their ability to perform as a prime contractor, joint venture, or subcontracting team, distinguish their own capability from that of team members, and identify limitations within each task area addressed. NIH will assess capability separately for each area. To be considered capable of supporting a task area, respondents must demonstrate that their proposed performance arrangement meets the full capability requirements stated for that task area below. Capability in both areas is not required to respond. Partial capability is insufficient to be considered capable of supporting the full task area. The Government has not made a final set-aside determination. Background The National Institutes of Health (NIH) conducts and supports biomedical and behavioral research to advance scientific knowledge and improve health. NIH requires professional, scientific, and technical contractor support for current and emerging research priorities, ongoing research activities, and related program operations. Changes in research programs and scientific methods create a continuing need for flexible service delivery and specialized expertise. Scientific & Technical Expertise Acquisition & Management (STEAM) will acquire contractor-provided services and expertise to accomplish varied project-based requirements across NIH. Individual task orders will define project objectives, tasks, deliverables or milestones, performance periods, required expertise, and resource needs. Contractors must furnish and manage the resources needed to perform multiple concurrent projects at substantial volume and adjust those resources as authorized project requirements change. NIH anticipates using cost-reimbursement contracting approximately 20 percent of the time. The actual mix will depend on individual requirements. Firms should describe their experience and ability to support this component, including any preparation needed. Existing cost-reimbursement capability or a prior Government accounting-system approval is not a mandatory condition of responding to this notice. Applicable requirements, including accounting-system adequacy, would need to be satisfied before award of a cost-reimbursement order. Purpose and Objectives The purpose of STEAM is to provide professional, scientific, and technical support for NIH research and related activities. Support includes basic, translational, and clinical research; vaccine research; general and specialized laboratory research; veterinary and animal research support; bioinformatics; computational biology; and related professional and technical services. The contractor will furnish and manage qualified resources to accomplish each statement of work (SOW), including responsibility for recruiting, verifying qualifications, retaining its personnel, and maintaining continuity of performance. Services will be furnished under individual funded, project-based task orders. The contractor will furnish resources, including personnel with expertise corresponding to the applicable labor categories, to accomplish the SOW and deliver the required project outcomes and milestones. The contractor will retain responsibility for employing, supervising, and managing its personnel. Services will not include inherently governmental functions or unauthorized personal services. Each task order will identify the applicable task area, project scope, qualifications, location, performance schedule, and security and safety requirements. Project Requirements Services may involve expertise in microbiology, molecular biology, biochemistry, infectious diseases, immunology, clinical research, bioinformatics, genomic sequencing, proteomics, image analysis, computational and systems biology, and scientific data analysis. Related requirements may include clinical trials support, laboratory operations, veterinary services, program management, and other professional or technical support within the authorized scope. Qualifications range from positions without a degree requirement to licensed practitioners and highly specialized doctoral-level professionals. The contractor must be able to furnish qualified resources within the task area or areas addressed and manage a substantial volume of concurrent project requirements. Primary anticipated locations include Bethesda and Rockville, Maryland; other locations in the Washington, DC metropolitan area; and Hamilton, Montana. Other domestic locations, overseas support, travel, or remote work may be authorized by individual orders. NIH-wide demand for task orders and contractor support fluctuates across projects, locations, and time. This notice does not provide a fixed annual volume estimate or guarantee a minimum workload. Routine task orders will establish mobilization, onboarding, and performance start schedules. Under certain circumstances, an urgent or unforeseen NIH need may require the contractor to begin authorized performance within 48 hours. For an expedited request, NIH will identify the applicable timeframe and the event from which it is measured. Respondents should describe their ability to accommodate these requests, identify the categories and locations they could support, and explain any limitations or prerequisites. Contractors must ensure that their personnel have the qualifications and relevant experience required for the assigned work and complete applicable training, competency verification, occupational health requirements, and facility-specific access approvals before beginning restricted work. For assignments involving regulated select agents or toxins, applicable individual access approvals, security risk assessments, and required training must be completed before access. Prior experience at another laboratory does not establish authorization at the receiving NIH facility. An expedited task-order request does not waive these prerequisites. The following 156 labor-category families are organized into two task areas. Each family appears once. Categories encompass applicable levels and specialties; task orders will specify required duties and qualifications. Numbered levels are not automatically equivalent to Junior, Mid-Level, or Senior designations. The task-area structure supports market research and does not establish the final award structure. Task Area A � Professional Services This area covers general professional, management, administrative, business, IT, and technical support for NIH projects, including project coordination, financial analysis, enterprise systems, and related operational services. Scientific versions of otherwise general roles are assigned to Task Area B. title: Request for Information - Multi-X Security (MXS) Platform Operations and Maintenance
description: Request for Information Multi-X Security (MXS) Platform Operations and Maintenance 15 October 2026 1.0 Description The Air Force Life Cycle Management Center, in support of the Advanced Technology Branch (AFLCMC/HNJT), is seeking information from interested companies with the capability to provide Operations and Maintenance, and continuous modernization of the Multi-X Security (MXS) Platform. 2.0 Background Between 2019 and 2026, the Advanced Technology program office developed the MXS (pronounced �Maxis�) Platform as a modern security model, data model, reference architecture, and reference implementation, based on open standards and protocols to support software development and secure information sharing at multiple security levels. MXS' goal is to enable Protection Level 3 (PL3) software solution development by third-party developers within security-constrained environments, as typically employed by communities working with Special Access Programs (SAPs). 3.0 Description of Requirements 3.1 Scope & Operating Environment: AFLCMC/HNJT requires information on industry capabilities to operate, maintain, and continuously enhance a multi-tenant, cloud-native platform supporting Air Force and mission-partner applications. The platform operates across multiple security enclaves, including Unclassified, Secret//Special Access Required (SAR), Top Secret//SAR, and Top Secret//Sensitive Compartmented Information (SCI)//SAR cloud environments. 3.2 Platform Operations, Maintenance & DevSecOps: Prospective contractors are expected to provide proactive 24/7/365 system availability, platform administration, and lifecycle sustainment across all designated cloud environments. Core focus areas include: 3.2.1 Cloud-Native Infrastructure: Operating and maintaining containerized environments (e.g., Kubernetes), service meshes, Application Programming Interface (API) gateways, and Infrastructure-as-Code (IaC) baselines. 3.2.2 DevSecOps Toolchain: Sustaining an automated continuous integration/continuous delivery (CI/CD) pipeline that enables secure cross-domain software progression. 3.2.3 Telemetry & Resource Monitoring: Providing automated, granular visibility into platform health, microservice performance, compute/storage utilization, and licensing. 3.2.4 Enterprise ICAM & Certificate Services: operate and maintain enterprise identity management infrastructure across multiple tenants. 3.2.5 Managed Database Services, Registered Queries & API Mediation: Provision, sustain, and optimize managed database services across cloud environments, engineer registered and parameterized queries for controlled data access and governance, and diagnose latency or throughput bottlenecks. 3.3 Continuous Platform Evolution: Delivering agile enhancements, feature updates, and technical debt remediation in alignment with government-prioritized backlogs. 3.4 Tenant Enablement & Multi-Tier Support: To support diverse tenant software programs, the platform requires integrated customer enablement services. 3.4.1 Tenant Onboarding and Offboarding: Assisting tenant developer teams with architectural guidance, common control inheritance, and standardized integration toolkits. 3.4.2 Service Desk Operations: Operating a tiered technical service desk (Tier 1�3) providing incident management, troubleshooting, and user assistance across all classification levels. 3.5 Cybersecurity & Continuous Authorization: The platform must maintain a rigorous cybersecurity posture compliant with DoD, Intelligence Community, and SAP directives. 3.5.1 Sustaining existing Risk Management Framework (RMF) Authorizations to Operate (ATOs). 3.5.2 Executing Static Application Security Testing (SAST) and Dynamic Application Security Testing (DAST), container vulnerability assessments, dependency assessments (Software Bill of Materials (SBOM), Vulnerability Exploitability eXchange (VeX), etc.), and rapid vulnerability remediation. 3.5.3 Generating and maintaining RMF bodies of evidence and security documentation to maintain inheritance relationships for hosted software and systems. 3.6 Potential Security, Facility, and Personnel Requirements. The Government is conducting market research regarding the availability, timing, and feasibility of contractor personnel clearances, secure facilities, and cybersecurity qualifications that may be required for a future acquisition. The requirements of any future solicitation, including timing and acceptability of facilities, will be established only in that solicitation. 3.6.1 Personnel Clearances: Contractor personnel must possess active Top Secret clearances and applicable DoD 8140 baseline certifications at the time of contract award, with the ability to obtain SCI and SAP access within 30 days of contract award 3.6.2 Secure Facilities: Within 30 days of contract award, the Contractor shall possess and maintain accredited Sensitive Compartmented Information Facility (SCIFs)/Special Access Program Facility (SAPFs), as required to perform the classified development and operational activities under this contract. Each facility shall maintain current written accreditation by the cognizant accrediting authority and comply with applicable requirements of ICD 705, DoDM 5105.21, Volume 2, and DoDM 5205.07. 4.0 Specific Areas of Interest 4.1 Corporate Overview & Business Classification 4.1.1 Entity Identification: State your company name, Commercial and Government Entity (CAGE) code, and business size/socioeconomic status under the designated North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code. 4.1.2 Contract Vehicles: List the relevant Government-Wide Acquisition Contracts (GWACs), Multiple Award Schedules (e.g., GSA MAS, NASA SEWP, OASIS+), or agency vehicles your organization currently holds. 4.2 Experience & Technical Approach 4.2.1 Relevant Past Performance: Provide up to three (3) examples (within the past 5 years) demonstrating prime or major subcontractor experience operating multi-tenant cloud platforms of comparable scope, complexity, and classification (including Amazon Web Services (AWS)/Azure Secret, Top Secret, or SAP enclaves). 4.2.2 Platform Management & DevSecOps: Describe your experience managing cloud-native infrastructure (e.g., Kubernetes, service mesh, Infrastructure as Code (IaC)) and sustaining multi-fabric DevSecOps pipelines across air-gapped or cross-domain environments. 4.2.3 Platform Software Development Kits (SDKs) & Toolkits: Summarize your experience developing and sustaining SDKs, shared libraries, and developer modules to accelerate tenant application delivery. 4.2.4 Enterprise Identity, Credential, and Access Management (ICAM) & Certificate Services: Describe your experience deploying and sustaining enterprise and external Certificate Authorities (CAs) across multi-tenant and air-gapped environments, including certificate validation and revocation infrastructure (e.g., Online Certificate Status Protocol (OCSP) responders, Certificate Revocation List (CRL) distribution points). 4.2.5 Managed Database Services, Registered Queries & API Mediation: Describe your experience provisioning, optimizing, and troubleshooting cloud-managed database services, including engineering registered and parameterized queries for controlled access and governance. Detail your experience developing middleware, abstraction layers, or gateway adapters for protocol bridging, query translation, and data transformation across disparate APIs. 4.2.6 Protection Level 3 (PL-3) Multi-Level Access Control & Attribute-Based Authorization: Describe your experience engineering and operating applications within PL3 SAR environments to restrict data access to users' explicit clearance and compartment authorizations. Detail your approach to synchronizing identity attributes from Authoritative Data Sources (ADS) and implementing, enforcing, and auditing Role-Based Access Control (RBAC), Mandatory Access Control (MAC), and Attribute-Based Access Control (ABAC) policies using Policy Enforceme

description: *** Q&A from Industry Day posted https://piee.eb.mil/sol/xhtml/unauth/search/oppMgmtLink.xhtml?noticeId=N0017827R3002&noticeType=SourcesSought **** NAVAL SURFACE WARFARE CENTER DAHLGREN DIVISION ADVANCE NOTICE / SOURCES SOUGHT A DEPT INFRASTRUCTURE, LIBRARY AND SYSTEMS ADMINISTRATION SUPPORT N0017827R3002 Summary of Requirement: The Naval Surface Warfare Center Dahlgren Division (NSWCDD) is an engineering, software development, and systems test and integration center for Research, Development, Test & Evaluation (RDT&E) components of the United States (U.S.) Navy. The Strategic and Computing Systems Department (A Department) provides system administration, networking and Integrated Logistics Support (ILS), infrastructure, library support services, systems engineering, software development and test and evaluation capabilities to various program offices and projects. The various commands include, but are not limited to, Naval Sea Systems Command (NAVSEA), Naval Air Systems Command (NAVAIR), Marine Corps System Command (MARCORSYSCOM), Strategic Systems Programs (SSP), and Joint Cyber Command & Control (JCC2). Projects include weapons control systems and warfare systems, notably, Submarine Launched Ballistic Missile (SLBM), Ship Submersible Ballistic Nuclear (SSBN), Submersible Ship Guided Nuclear (SSGN), Strategic Weapons System (SWS), Submarine Launched Cruise Missile - Nuclear (SLCM-N), Tomahawk Weapons System (TWS), Tactical Tomahawk Weapon Control System (TTWCS), Aegis (both land- and sea-based), the Ship Self-Defense System (SSDS), United States Coast Guard Cutters, DDG-1000 Guided Missile Destroyers, Combined Integrated Air and Missile Defense Anti-Submarine Warfare Trainer (CIAT), Guided Missile Frigate (FFG(X)) ships, other tactical Navy and Marine Corps programs, and cyberspace programs including the Mission Assurance Decision Support System (MADSS). The overall focus of the NSWCDD A Department has grown and changed over time to broaden its scope to include any weapons system/weapons control system programs, combat systems, and other complex engineering systems. As such, A Department requires versatile and in-depth system administration and Integrated Logistics Support (ILS), infrastructure, library and support services throughout each of its organizational units with extensive experience in all aspects explained in this Statement of Work (SOW). Work Locations and Full Time Equivalents (FTEs): It is anticipated a total of 206 FTEs will be needed (excluding Surge SLINs) under the Cost-Plus-Fixed-Fee (CPFF) Contract Line Item No. (CLINs): 34 FTEs for the Base Year (BY), 41 FTEs for Option Year (OY) one (1), 41 FTEs for OY two (2), 43 FTEs for OY three (3), and 47 FTEs for OY four (4); and 210 FTEs under the Fixed-Price (FP) CLIN: 38 FTEs for the BY, 40 for OY one (1), 44 for OY two (2), 45 for OY three (3), and 45 for OY four (4). The resultant order will have a Base Period of twelve months, and four (4) Option Periods each consisting of twelve months each, for a total of 60 months, if all Options are exercised. Set-Aside: At this time, a determination has NOT been made to set-aside this procurement. Responses to this Sources Sought will be evaluated and used to determine the set-aside status of this requirement. Incumbent: This follow-on work consolidates CPFF Task Order N0017819D8647/N0017821F3003 (Tatitlek Technologies, Inc., 561 East 36th Ave. Anchorage, AK 99503) and CPFF Task Order N0017819D8413/N0017821F3013 (Resource Management Concepts, 46970 Bradley Blvd, Suite B Lexington Park, MD). Personnel and Facility Clearance Requirements: Contractors shall meet the following mandatory requirements at the time of proposal submission or have an acceptable plan to meet the requirements by the start date of contract performance. In addition, mandatory requirements must be maintained throughout the life of the Task Order. The mandatory requirements are as follows: Facility Clearance Level (FCL) Requirement: The Prime Contractor supporting this Task Order is required to have an FCL of TOP SECRET and safeguarding clearance level of SECRET at the primary facility supporting this Task Order. Personnel Clearance Level (PCL) Requirement: All personnel directly supporting this Task Order, except Management and Support personnel, are required to have, as a minimum, a current SECRET security clearance in the Defense Industrial Security System (DISS). Interim clearances are acceptable. Personnel performing in the following labor categories shall have a final TOP SECRET security clearance in DISS: Library Specialist (1 FTE) SR Systems Administrator (6 FTEs) Systems Administrator (3 FTEs) Senior Network Administrator (1 FTE) Network Administrator (4 FTEs). Identify whether individuals are employees of the Offeror, are contingent hires, or are employees of a planned team member (Sub-contractor). If employees are those of a planned team member, the name of the Sub-contractor shall also be identified. (4) A description of the Offeror's ability to meet each of the Personnel and Facility Clearance requirements in SOW Section C.8.1 by time of award. (5) Specific past performance on same or similar size and scope of work performed by the Offeror as a prime Contractor under a Government contract within the past five (5) years, including a description of the services provided, the dollar value of the effort, and the contract number. title: Replace DSN-HDD Generator for 78th Signal Battalion, Camp Zama, Japan.
description: This Statement of Work (SOW) defines the requirements, scope, responsibilities, and deliverables for the replacement and disposal of the 150kVA emergency power diesel generator located on Camp Zama Japan Building 121. This is a solicitation for commercial products or commercial services prepared in accordance with the format in FAR 12 as supplemented with additional information included in this notice. The written solicitation, issued as SF1449 (Form), is attached to this notice and constitutes the official solicitation. Quotes are being requested in accordance with the instructions herein and within the attached SF1449. The statements required by FAR 12.202(b)(1) are included in the uploaded documents. Expecting award date is around 30 Oct 2026 (subject to change). Description of Services: The contractor shall provide all necessary labor, management, tools, equipment, transportation, and materials to perform the decommissioning, removal, disposal, and replacement of the existing 150kVA emergency power diesel generator at Building 121, Camp Zama, Japan. The primary objective is to safely disconnect and dispose of the existing unserviceable generator (Toyo Denki Seizo / TYND-215) and install a brand new 150 kVA / 120 kW diesel generator (208/120 VAC, 50 Hz). The new system must be fully integrated and compatible with the existing Automatic Transfer Switch (ATS) in Panel P-M/L-M. The project includes full testing, an 8-hour load test, commissioning, and training. All disposal of the old generator and hazardous materials must comply with Japanese environmental regulations utilizing off-base facilities. A minimum 2-year warranty is required for the new generator system. The contractor is required to provide employees who have demonstrated experience in work like this requirement. The contractor or their sub-contractors shall ensure their employees have the following current and valid professional certifications for the entire life of this contract: Special Electric Officer's License (for Emergency Power Generators) (????????? - ???????????) Chief Electrical Engineer (Licensed Class I, II, or III) (???????) Fire Defense Equipment Officer (?????) Low-Voltage Electrical Worker Special Education (????????????) Failure to submit verifiable evidence of these qualifications and certifications at the time of quote submission may result in the offer being evaluated as technically unacceptable. Note 1: All work for this project shall be performed exclusively in Japan. The contract price shall be inclusive of all travel and lodging expenses required for project execution. Note 2: Mandatory On-Site Warranty & Local Service Capability The project and product utilization will occur entirely within the country of Japan. During the Warranty Period, the selected contractor must provide on-site repair, troubleshooting, or replacement services at the Off-Post locations in Japan. Note 3: If the offeror is not physically located in Japan, the offeror MUST submit documentation demonstrating an established partnership with a local authorized service provider in Japan capable of meeting all on-site requirements. Please provide the partner company�s Name, Address, Point of Contact, Email, and Phone Number with your quote. Failure to submit verifiable evidence of local warranty service capability at the time of quote submission will result in the offer being evaluated as technically unacceptable and not considered for award. Note 4: If successful offeror is a U.S. vendor, resulting contract will include DFARS clause 252.225-7976, Contractor Personnel Performing in Japan (Deviation 2018-O0019). The clause requires DoD contractors to account for contractor personnel and dependents in the Synchronized Predeployment and Operational Tracker (SPOT), in order for the contractor personnel and dependents to be eligible for coverage under the Status of Forces Agreement. Note 5: Trade Agreements Act (TAA) Compliance & Prohibited Sources This procurement is subject to the Trade Agreements Act (TAA). Quotes will be evaluated IAW DFARS 252.225-7020, FAR 52.212-1 and 52.212-2. Note 6: Site Visit. A pre-solicitation site visit is scheduled to be conducted on 7 October 2026, at 10:00 AM (JST) at Camp Zama, Japan. All prospective quoters are strongly encouraged to attend. To participate, submit a list of all attendees (including full name, residential address, nationality, pass port number or driver�s license number) via email to hiroko.takahashi.jp@us.af.mil and kaori.kanematsu.jp@us.af.mil no later than 7 calendar days prior to the scheduled visit. Note 7: No additional site visit is scheduled.?

title: ICD-705 Controlled Spaces Modernization and Sustainment Program - (Progressive Design-build (PDB) Other Transaction Agreement (OTA)
description: SOURCES SOUGHT ANNOUNCEMENT AND INDUSTRY DAY NOTICE PROGRESSIVE DESIGN-BUILD (PDB) OTHER TRANSACTION AGREEMENT (OTA) ICD-705 Controlled Spaces Modernization and Sustainment Program Osan Air Base, Republic of Korea U.S. Army Corps of Engineers � Far East District DISCLAIMER: This Sources Sought is issued solely for market research/intelligence and acquisition planning. It is not a solicitation, Request for Qualifications, or commitment to issue a solicitation or award any agreement or contract. No Statements of Qualifications or proposals are requested. Participation is voluntary; the Government will not reimburse response costs and will not accept unsolicited proposals. Responses will inform acquisition strategy, industry capability assessment, and project delivery options. Responding does not affect eligibility for any future solicitation. THE OPPORTUNITY The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, Far East District (USACE FED) invites industry partners to help shape the acquisition strategy for a high-priority modernization and sustainment program involving ICD-705 controlled spaces at Osan Air Base, Republic of Korea. The Government is evaluating an innovative Progressive Design-Build (PDB) delivery method executed through an Other Transaction Agreement (OTA) under 10 U.S.C. � 2808a. This approach enables early contractor involvement, collaborative design development, open-book pricing, and flexible risk allocation�advantages particularly valuable for complex, security-sensitive work performed in an active overseas operational environment with unique host-nation and ICD-705 constraints. The Government has not made a final acquisition strategy determination and seeks candid industry input on the benefits, limitations, risks, and commercial terms of a PDB OTA compared with traditional design-bid-build or design-build approaches. WHY PROGRESSIVE DESIGN-BUILD / OTA? ICD-705 controlled spaces, collective protection systems, and HVAC modernization on an active air base present technical, security, operational, and logistical complexities that benefit from early industry engagement. A PDB OTA structure may allow: Joint refinement of requirements and design while the facility remains operational; Early identification and mitigation of long-lead items, host-nation interfaces, and ICD-705 accreditation risks; Transparent, open-book cost development leading to a more reliable construction baseline (including potential GMP); Flexible commercial terms and governance tailored to the unique constraints of overseas military construction in the Republic of Korea. The Government is particularly interested in industry�s practical experience with these methods on similar secure or operationally constrained projects, as well as any recommended alternatives that would better achieve mission, schedule, and cost objectives. PROJECT SCOPE The program encompasses modernization and sustainment work in two existing facilities at Osan Air Base: Building A � Collective Protection, HVAC & ICD-705 Modernization Replace the existing M49 Collective Protection System (CPS) filter system with a new M98 CPS, including associated blast doors, seals, relief valves, electronic control systems, and other appurtenances, fully coordinated with applicable ICD-705 requirements. Replace or modernize principal components of the existing HVAC system to support ICD-705 environmental and security standards. Convert approximately 2,610 square feet of existing space to meet applicable ICD-705 requirements. Building B � ICD-705 Conversion & Facility Sustainment Convert approximately 3,700 square feet of existing space to meet applicable ICD-705 requirements. Perform sustainment work on approximately 50,000 square feet, including roof repairs and existing office space improvements. Repair and/or replace components of the existing fire protection and fire alarm systems; air-handling units (AHUs), air-cooled condensing units (ACCUs), and associated HVAC infrastructure; bathroom fixtures and plumbing; plus associated incidental work required to complete the planned improvements. Estimated program magnitude: $60�100 million. Construction funding for both facilities is anticipated for obligation in FY27, subject to availability of funds and applicable approvals. This Sources Sought is the Government�s primary tool to assess industry interest, capability, and preferred commercial practices before finalizing the acquisition approach. ACQUISITION APPROACH UNDER EVALUATION Industry feedback will help refine potential agreement structure, project phasing, pricing approach, governance, risk allocation, and other commercial terms. Potential Phase 1 � Design and Preconstruction The Government and selected contractor would collaborate to refine project requirements, develop the design, conduct constructability reviews, identify long-lead equipment, evaluate phasing and operational constraints, obtain subcontractor input, develop cost estimates, and mitigate technical and execution risks. Feedback is requested on the design maturity, site investigations, pricing information, and agreement terms needed to establish a reliable construction cost and schedule baseline. Potential Phase 2 � Construction Following design development and resolution of key technical and commercial risks, the contractor may be asked to propose a construction price, potentially including a Guaranteed Maximum Price (GMP) if appropriate to the final structure. Any transition to construction would be subject to the terms of the resulting agreement, Government acceptance, availability of funds, and required approvals. The Government seeks practical recommendations for off-ramp provisions, design deliverables, compensation, and transition arrangements should the parties be unable to reach agreement on construction pricing or other required terms. Alternative acquisition strategies that industry believes would better support the program�s security, technical, schedule, cost, and operational requirements are welcome and encouraged. INDUSTRY DAY A Virtual Industry Day is to be determined. The SAM.gov posting will be updated with registration instructions and meeting information when available. Interested firms are strongly encouraged to add themselves to the Interested Vendors List associated with this announcement on SAM.gov to receive timely updates, including Industry Day details. INFORMATION REQUESTED FROM INDUSTRY Your candid, detailed feedback is critical to shaping a successful acquisition. The Government�s primary mechanism for obtaining market research is the Industry Questionnaire, which addresses capability and capacity, relevant experience, Progressive Design-Build experience, open-book pricing, technical capabilities (ICD-705, CPS, secure facilities), real estate and construction considerations in the Republic of Korea, schedule, security, risk, governance, and recommended commercial practices. 1. Complete the Industry Questionnaire: Access the Questionnaire Here (https://forms.osi.apps.mil/Pages/ResponsePage.aspx?id=unZN_HzxUEy5p48xY9J1gkOXdBFTSSpJlGbZL6EFB8NUN1FSQ0pXMEE3TU05UzlUQ09QNjNMSjNTTyQlQCN0PWcu) or complete the questionnaire attached. 2. Submit a Capability Statement (not to exceed 12 pages). Include: Company name and address, CAGE code and/or Unique Entity Identifier (UEI) from your SAM.gov registration. Clearly identify if you are a foreign firm, partner, or subsidiary located outside the United States. Business size status and any applicable socioeconomic categories under NAICS Code 236220 � Commercial and Institutional Building Construction (small business size standard: $45 million). Two completed projects of similar nature and complexity (examples: ICD-705 controlled spaces, collective protection system installation or modernization, secure facility conversion, complex HVAC/CPS upgrades in operational military facilities, or comparable high-security construction).
